lesson.title: Sensitive biometric categorisation
lesson.summary: Read the named sensitive-inference categories and the lawful-dataset/law-enforcement boundaries.

prerequisites.reason: The sensitive-attribute test applies to individual biometric categorisation.
The learner must check the listed inference purpose rather than infer a ban from the category name.

blocks: The **sensitive-categorisation ban** concerns categorising individual people from biometric data to deduce/infer race, political opinions, trade-union membership, religious/philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation.
Record the actual inferred category. The point's list is specific; do not silently substitute every imaginable attribute or ignore the biometric basis.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(40); Article 5(1)(g); Annex III 1(b)

blocks: The point excludes specified labelling/filtering of lawfully acquired biometric datasets based on biometric data, and categorising biometric data in law enforcement. Read these stated boundaries without turning them into blanket permission.
**Lawfully acquired** is a factual and legal condition. Public availability or an internal dataset label alone does not establish it. The precise processing purpose still matters.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(40); Article 5(1)(g); Annex III 1(b)

blocks: Fictional Northbridge case: a workplace tool infers union membership from individual facial data. Those stipulated sensitive-inference facts raise the named prohibition.

Changed case: an actual lawful-dataset filtering operation is established. Examine the boundary as written, then privacy and other rules. Do not use a dataset-management label to hide individual sensitive inference.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(40); Article 5(1)(g); Annex III 1(b)

blocks: A function outside this particular ban can still be a listed sensitive/protected categorisation under Annex III. Conversely, high-risk classification cannot authorise the prohibited inference.
The record should identify biometric data, individual categories, precise purpose, acquisition legality and regulated action. Keep each conclusion bounded to the actual processing.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 3(40); Article 5(1)(g); Annex III 1(b)
